children: Emma Tucker
1. FROM MY DESK
The Federal Aviation Administration halted U.S. flight departures Friday afternoon, underscoring the fragility of America's air-traffic control infrastructure.

The extraordinary step, triggered by telecommunications disruptions, was the most severe nationwide ground stop in the U.S. since Sept. 11, 2001. It threw airports into chaos and stranded tens of thousands of travelers. (Our travel columnist, Dawn Gilbertson, was in the air when the halt hit-but her 84-year-old mother wasn't so lucky.)

What caused the breakdown? Our reporters traced the issues to a single router at an FAA radio site in rural Arkansas. We have new details on what went wrong-and let you hear, through radio broadcasts and airline-pilot messages, how the four-hour saga unfolded.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST
Jensen Huang built the backdoor route that keeps Beijing in the AI race.

During his tenure as (Nvidia's) CEO, Huang built a multibillion-dollar business to feed the ravenous appetite of Chinese customers for American chips, cultivating a network of Asian partners who could serve the Chinese far from Washington's eyes. He befriended Trump and lobbied Washington hard to keep the backdoor to China open. China's AI developers exploited the Nvidia chips they desperately needed to catch up with America's leaders, either using smuggled chips or accessing them remotely in places like Malaysia. Revelations about Huang's affair with an executive at one of those Asian partners-a possible Chinese intelligence asset-didn't just blow up his career. They now threaten to implode the entire lucrative ecosystem he built in Asia, report Jon Emont, Stu Woo, Patricia Kowsmann and Raffaele Huang.
They're lucky enough to have a 3% mortgage-and feel like they can never move.

High mortgage rates have crushed homeowners' budgets and frozen the U.S. housing market. Some lucky Americans haven't felt any of it. Millions of homeowners secured historically low mortgage rates during the pandemic, either with a new home purchase or by refinancing an existing mortgage. The 30-year fixed mortgage rate currently stands at 7.1%. Homeowners with a 3% mortgage rate or lower look like anyone else. But there are tells: Some are buying luxury cars, booking expensive vacations and retiring early. They may keep silent, or slip out of the room when the topic of mortgage rates comes up in polite conversation. Some feel lucky, others feel trapped in homes they can't leave because they will never get a better deal, reports Rebecca Picciotto.

6. SEE THE STORY
There's a backyard battle happening over Amazon delivery drones 'stealing the sky.'

They rise early in Baton Rouge, La., like bees from a hive-in this case, an enormous (Amazon) fulfillment center. Fans watch as the Prime Air drones dart over trees, roads and power lines before they make a beeline to customers, descend in a rush of air and drop boxes onto their lawns. But all is not well in Dronesville. Some locals complain that the 80-pound drones sound more like flying leaf blowers and are destroying their peace and quiet, threatening people's privacy and driving away birds.

8. THE NUMBER

The share of their wealth that some newly minted AI millionaires aim to give away, according to wealth advisers. The urge to give is being fueled by mission-driven corporate cultures, as well as guilt about AI's potential harms. Wealth advisers looking to attract these millionaires are trotting out a new pitch: We can help you give your money away. That means showing they can structure charitable giving, align investments with clients' values and measure the impact of their money-or risk seeing their pitches fall flat.
